78978-the-coach-horn.title: The Coach Horn
78978-the-coach-horn.creator: Unknown
78978-the-coach-horn.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. A very worthy friend of mine, of no particular talent (although he can sound a Coach-horn right well, and drives his own four-in-hand), once asked me to play something on the violin, and when I had done so, he observed, “Ah, I learnt the fiddle when I was young, and should have played very nicely indeed, if I had taken the trouble.”

arxiv-2105-13031.title: Geodesy of irregular small bodies via neural density fields: geodesyNets
arxiv-2105-13031.creator: Dario Izzo, Pablo Gómez
arxiv-2105-13031.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Dario Izzo, Pablo Gómez. Asteroids’ and comets’ geodesy is of increasing interest in a wide range of fields ranging from astronomy to potential future mining prospects, as well as being essential to successful proximity operations of spacecraft. However, the problem of inferring the internal density distribution of irregular bodies from gravity measurements is challenging and ill posed, with the added difficulty of finding compact representations of the gravitational field surrounding them.

arxiv-2206-12753.title: Spatiotemporal Data Mining: A Survey DOI: 10.1145/1122445.1122456 Journal: JACM Volume: 37 4 1 8 CCS: Information Systems Spatiotemporal Data Mining, Spatial Data Mining CCS: Computing Methodologies Parallel Computing
arxiv-2206-12753.creator: Arun Sharma, Zhe Jiang, Shashi Shekhar
arxiv-2206-12753.description: Abstract . Spatiotemporal data mining aims to discover interesting, useful but non-trivial patterns in big spatial and spatiotemporal data. They are used in various application domains such as public safety, ecology, epidemiology, earth science etc. This problem is challenging because of the high societal cost of spurious patterns and exorbitant computational cost.

arxiv-2303-11789.title: Decentralized Online Learning for Random Inverse Problems Over Graphs
arxiv-2303-11789.creator: Tao Li, Xiwei Zhang, Yan Chen
arxiv-2303-11789.description: Abstract We propose a decentralized online learning algorithm for distributed random inverse problems over network graphs with online measurements, and unify the distributed parameter estimation in Hilbert spaces and the least mean square problem in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHS-LMS).

arxiv-2404-14074.title: Towards Proxy Staking Accounts Based on NFTs in Ethereum
arxiv-2404-14074.creator: Viktor Valaštín, Roman Bitarovský, Kristián Košťál and Ivan Kotuliak
arxiv-2404-14074.description: Abstract Blockchain is a technology that is often used to share data and assets. However, in the decentralized ecosystem, blockchain-based systems can be utilized to share information and assets without the traditional barriers associated with solo responsibility, e.g., multi-sig wallets. This paper describes an innovative approach to blockchain networks based on a non-fungible token that behaves as an account (NFTAA).

arxiv-2406-14986.title: Implicit Probabilistic Reasoning Does Not Reflect Explicit Answers in Large Language Models
arxiv-2406-14986.creator: Manuel Mondal manuel.mondal@unifr.ch, Ljiljana Dolamic ljiljana.dolamic@armasuisse.ch, Gérôme Bovet gerome.bovet@armasuisse.ch, Philippe Cudré-Mauroux philippe.cudre-mauroux@unifr.ch, Julien Audiffren julien.audiffren@unifr.ch
arxiv-2406-14986.description: Abstract The handling of probabilities in the form of uncertainty or partial information is an essential task for LLMs in many settings and applications. A common approach to evaluate an LLM’s probabilistic reasoning capabilities is to assess its ability to answer questions pertaining to probability through the use of multiple-choice questions (MCQs).

arxiv-2504-21376.creator: Ye Yan 1, Qi Huang 1, Qian Wu 2,3, Hongxia Huang 1, Jialun Ping 1
arxiv-2504-21376.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ye Yan 1, Qi Huang 1, Qian Wu 2,3, Hongxia Huang 1, Jialun Ping 1. Inspired by recent researches on the p ​ Ω p\Omega and p ​ Λ ¯ p\bar{\Lambda} systems, we investigate the p ​ Ω ¯ p\bar{\Omega} systems within the framework of a quark model.

arxiv-2505-18463.title: CHSER: A Dataset and Case Study on Generative Speech Error Correction for Child ASR
arxiv-2505-18463.creator: Natarajan, Zilai, Kaiyuan, Mohan, Abeer
arxiv-2505-18463.description: Abstract Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems struggle with child speech due to its distinct acoustic and linguistic variability and limited availability of child speech datasets, leading to high transcription error rates. While ASR error correction (AEC) methods have improved adult speech transcription, their effectiveness on child speech remains largely unexplored.

arxiv-2507-08055.title: MCPmed: A Call for MCP-Enabled Bioinformatics Web Services for LLM-Driven Discovery
arxiv-2507-08055.creator: Matthias Flotho, Ian Ferenc Diks, Philipp Flotho, Leidy-Alejandra G. Molano, Pascal Hirsch, Andreas Keller
arxiv-2507-08055.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Matthias Flotho, Ian Ferenc Diks, Philipp Flotho, Leidy-Alejandra G. Molano, Pascal Hirsch, Andreas Keller. Bioinformatics web servers are critical resources in modern biomedical research, facilitating interactive exploration of datasets through custom-built interfaces with rich visualization capabilities. However, this human-centric design limits machine readability for large language models (LLMs) and deep research agents. We address this gap by adapting the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to bioinformatics web server backends—a standardized, machine-actionable layer that explicitly associates webservice endpoints with scientific concepts and detailed metadata.

arxiv-2510-24981.title: Star Quasiconvexity: an Unified Approach for Linear Convergence of First-Order Methods Beyond Convexity
arxiv-2510-24981.creator: Phan Quoc Khanh, Felipe Lara
arxiv-2510-24981.description: Abstract We introduce a class of generalized convex functions, termed star quasiconvexity, to ensure the linear convergence of gradient and proximal point methods. This class encompasses convex, star-convex, quasiconvex, and quasar-convex functions. We establish that a function is star quasiconvex if and only if all its sublevel sets are star-shaped with respect to the set of its minimizers.

arxiv-2512-00668.title: Restricted Block Permutation for Two-Sample Testing
arxiv-2512-00668.creator: Jungwoo Ho
arxiv-2512-00668.description: Abstract We study a structured permutation scheme for two-sample testing that restricts permutations to single cross-swaps between block-selected representatives. Our analysis yields three main results. First, we provide an exact validity construction that applies to any fixed restricted permutation set.

arxiv-2601-11724.title: SemAlign: Language Guided Semi-supervised Domain Generalization
arxiv-2601-11724.creator: Muditha Fernando, Kajhanan Kailainathan, Krishnakanth Nagaratnam, Isuranga Udaravi Bandara Senavirathne, Ranga Rodrigo
arxiv-2601-11724.description: Abstract Semi-supervised Domain Generalization (SSDG) addresses the challenge of generalizing to unseen target domains with limited labeled data. Existing SSDG methods highlight the importance of achieving high pseudo-labeling (PL) accuracy and preventing model overfitting as the main challenges in SSDG.

arxiv-2601-16376.title: PolyAgent: Large Language Model Agent for Polymer Design
arxiv-2601-16376.creator: Vani Nigam, Achuth Chandrasekhar, Amir Barati Farimani
arxiv-2601-16376.description: Abstract On-demand Polymer discovery is essential for various industries, ranging from biomedical to reinforcement materials. Experiments with polymers have a long trial-and-error process, leading to a long time and extensive resources. For these processes, machine learning has accelerated scientific discovery at the property prediction and latent space search fronts.

arxiv-2602-11147.title: Let Leaders Play Games: Improving Timing in Leader-based Consensus
arxiv-2602-11147.creator: Rasheed M, Parth Desai, Sujit Gujar
arxiv-2602-11147.description: Abstract Propagation latency is inherent to any distributed network, including blockchains. Typically, blockchain protocols provide a timing buffer for block propagation across the network. In leader-based blockchains, the leader – block proposer – is known in advance for each slot.

pmc-10547701.creator: Atta ur Rahman, Hazrat Ali, S. M. Zangi, Cong-Feng Qiao
pmc-10547701.description: The preservation of quantum correlations requires optimal procedures and the proper design of the transmitting channels. pmc-10573489.title: Non-Contrast MR Lymphography and Intranodal Dynamic Contrast MR Lymphangiography in Children with Congenital Heart Disease—Imaging Findings as well as Impact on Patient Management and Outcome
pmc-10573489.creator: Christoph Bauer, Mario Scala, Pavel Sekyra, Franz Fellner, Gerald Tulzer, Silvia S Barbieri
pmc-10573489.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Lymphatic flow disorders are rare but devastating complications in children with congenital heart disease. T2-weighted magnetic resonance lymphography and intranodal dynamic contrast magnetic resonance lymphangiography are imaging modalities that can depict central lymphatic anatomy and flow pattern.

pmc-10607865.title: Evaluating Retinal Disease Diagnosis with an Interpretable Lightweight CNN Model Resistant to Adversarial Attacks
pmc-10607865.creator: Mohan Bhandari, Tej Bahadur Shahi, Arjun Neupane, P Jidesh, Vasudevan (Vengu) Lakshminarayanan
pmc-10607865.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) is an imperative symptomatic tool empowering the diagnosis of retinal diseases and anomalies. The manual decision towards those anomalies by specialists is the norm, but its labor-intensive nature calls for more proficient strategies. Consequently, the study recommends employing a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for the classification of OCT images derived from the OCT dataset into distinct categories, including Choroidal NeoVascularization (CNV), Diabetic Macular Edema (DME), Drusen, and Normal.

pmc-12618940.title: Intrinsic dysfunction in muscle stem cells lacking dystrophin begins during secondary myogenesis
pmc-12618940.creator: Marie E. Esper, Alexander Y. T. Lin, Dallas Bennett, Michael A. Rudnicki
pmc-12618940.description: Loss of dystrophin causes Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD), a neuromuscular disease characterized by muscle fragility and muscle stem cell (MuSC) impairment. Conventional understanding is that DMD manifests after birth from cumulative muscle damage. Here, examination of mdx mouse embryos lacking dystrophin reveals no impairment of the primary myogenic program.

pmc-13003600.title: Mental health burden and service barriers among medical and health sciences students: prevalence and determinants from a cross-sectional analysis
pmc-13003600.creator: Shaimaa M. Hassan, Najeeb M. Alqahtani, Salihah M. Alshahrani, Aser M. Abuelnasr, Abdulkhalig A. Alhefzy, Khaled W. Al Assiri, Bandar W. Al Assiri, Omar S. Alharthi, Muhannad M. Alharbi
pmc-13003600.description: BackgroundMedical and health sciences students face significant academic, clinical, and social pressures that increase their risk of psychological distress. Prior studies report elevated levels of depression, anxiety, and stress in this group. Barriers to accessing mental health services such as stigma, confidentiality concerns, limited awareness, and fear of negative consequences further compound this risk.

pmc-13407187.title: Harnessing human immune system models to validate NADPH oxidase 1 inhibition as treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma
pmc-13407187.creator: Zenzi De Vos, Lander Heyerick, Aline Baekelandt, Lara Morren, Anne Hoorens, Hasan Eker, Luís Abreu de Carvalho, Filip Gryspeerdt, Frederik Berrevoet, Hannah Stocks, Andy Wullaert, Sarah Raevens, Anja Geerts, Xavier Verhelst, Sander Lefere, Hans Van Vlierberghe, Lindsey Devisscher
pmc-13407187.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionNADPH oxidase 1 inhibition (NOX1i) has shown to alter the tumor microenvironment in conventional mouse models for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, clinical translation is hampered by low translatability of these models.MethodsWe developed two novel human immune system (HIS) mouse models, co-transplanted with orthotopic human HCC cells, to investigate NOX1i in the context of human HCC and human adaptive (T cell-HIS-HCC) or innate (Myeloid-HIS-HCC) immune responses. Mice received NOX1i or vehicle twice per week for 3 weeks.
